summary: Discovery focused on fallback acceptance criteria, multi-region routing, and whether Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private can meet Sable Energy's compliance and latency SLOs. Discussed K-V cache behavior, graceful degradation, and oncall responsibilities; agreed next steps for a short benchmark and security handoff.
questions: What does automatic fallback look like for us-east -> us-west?
Can Dedicated meet our latency P95 under 200ms?
How are audit logs surfaced for Private deployments?
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-16 11:00 AM PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Gupta (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Solutions) -- Ruth Delgado (CTO), Ian Park (Platform), Lea Morris (Security), Tom Becker (SRE)
---
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving time.
[00:12] Ruth: thanks Ethan, yeah we wanna get into how you handle outages and what the fallback acceptance is, we've had a few incidents where model endpoints degraded and we need bounded user impact.
[00:22] Ethan: totally. so high level we support Hosted, Dedicated, and Private — and the fallback story is policy driven. Maya, wanna walk through the routing model?
[00:30] Maya: sure. so think of routing as a route table: each route has priority, threshold SLOs, and then a fallback chain. primary can be region A on Redwood Hosted model variant, fallback to Dedicated pool in region B, then optionally to a smaller quantized variant, or finally to a cached response/backoff.
[00:51] Ian: when you say cached response what are we talking about? we can't just return stale stuff for billing queries, that's dangerous.
[00:58] Maya: right, so we have prefix/KV cache — apologies transcription note, sometimes the export shows K-V cash — it's a per-route cache with TTLs and validation. For low-risk content we can return cached partials, but for sensitive billing answers we recommend explicit no-cache and a stricter fallback like model variant with deterministic outputs.
[01:20] Ruth: okay. what's the observable? how do we know a fallback happened?
[01:25] Maya: every request includes a routing trace id and we surface fallback events in Redwood Console. you get per-request fallback reason (node OOM, model degraded latency, region down), and token-level latency breakdown.
[01:39] Lea: on audit logs — if we go Private in our VPC, do we still get the same detail? and does KMS integrate with our HSM?
[01:47] Ethan: yes, Private ships the same telemetry to your control plane; logs can be pushed to your SIEM via a syslog/HTTPS forwarder, and for key mgmt we support external KMS/HSM integrations (customers have brought HashiCorp Vault and AWS KMS).
[02:03] Tom: what's the SLA we can expect for Dedicated? our internal target is 99.95% regional uptime and p95 under 200ms for generate endpoints at peak.
[02:12] Maya: Dedicated comes with contractual SLOs — typical is 99.9% availability but we can discuss higher tiers on reserved pools and 24/7 support. latency depends on model size and batching; with config tuning we often hit p95 ~150-220ms for 8k context smaller models, but for larger context or beefier models it's higher.
[02:36] Ian: clarify batching — does Redwood batch across tenants? we need tenant isolation and predictable latencies.
[02:42] Maya: no cross-tenant batching on Dedicated. Dedicated uses isolated GPU pools and batching is constrained by policy; you can set max batch latency and size to control tail. Hosted may use multi-tenant batching which is why tails can vary.
[02:58] Ruth: and for grace periods — say a model cold starts or there's degradation, is the fallback immediate or do you have a ramp?
[03:05] Maya: it's configurable. you can set a soft threshold where we slow traffic (queueing/backpressure) and then an aggressive failover threshold where we shift traffic to fallback. also support canary windows for rollouts and automatic rollback on error spikes.
[03:20] Ethan: wanted to flag a common customer ask — simulate partial region degradation rather than full outage. we support partial-fault injection during tests, and we can run traffic split experiments to validate graceful degradation.
[03:32] Tom: perfect. one more question on multi-region routing — how deterministic is region steering? e.g., country-level routing and latency-based steering.
[03:41] Maya: routing policies include geo-IP rules, latency probes, and cost weightings. region steering is heuristic + health checks; you can pin a customer group to a region with automatic failover if health drops below X.
[03:54] Ian: any hard limits on failing over KV caches? does the cache warm-up cause a spike in latency?
[04:01] Maya: cache warm-up can increase RPS to the model; we recommend a warmed standby or using warmed KV snapshots. there are also pre-warming hooks that can be triggered during planned failover.
[04:12] Ruth: security — need SOC2, ISO, SSO with SCIM provisioning, and audit trails. can Redwood provide artifacts?
[04:18] Ethan: yes, we'll share the security pack. we are SOC2 Type II, and for Private we support SAML/SSO with SCIM groups and RBAC.
[04:28] Lea: do you have attestations around data residency? we operate in EMEA and need customer data to remain in eu-west-1 for certain workloads.
[04:36] Maya: we have region pinning and can run Private in a customer VPC in eu-west-1, or Hosted with data residency controls where model state and logs for that workload remain in-region.
[04:48] Tom: incident responsibilities — if a model OOMs in Dedicated, who owns rollback and support during off hours?
[04:55] Ethan: depends on plan. with enterprise reserved Dedicated you get 24/7 support and an SE on-call; otherwise it's business hours with escalation paths. but our platform can auto-fallback to a quantized variant minimizing customer impact while engineers investigate.
[05:10] Ian: curious about cost tradeoffs — moving to a smaller quantized variant as fallback, does that materially change output quality? we care about hallucination for billing language.
[05:20] Maya: quantized variants can introduce slight quality deltas; we recommend running evals on your prompt set and Redwood Optimize can recommend which quantization recipe keeps acceptable BLEU/metric delta while saving cost. for safety-critical outputs we typically avoid quantized fallback or add faster but deterministic post-checks.
[05:36] Ruth: interesting. can you show us a simple acceptance criteria matrix we can use? like what constitutes acceptable user-visible degradation?
[05:44] Ethan: yes. typical matrix rows: functional correctness (no PII leak), latency p95 threshold delta, error-rate threshold, freshness constraints (cache TTL), and auditability. e.g., allowed: p95 up to +100ms, error-rate <0.5% sustained, degrade to cached response only if non-financial.
[06:05] Ruth: we'd like that in writing. also want to see a sample runbook for failover.
[06:10] Ethan: we'll include a runbook template with playbook steps: detect, alert, failover, rollback, postmortem. Jordan will add the specific telemetry keys.
[06:20] Jordan: quick note: telemetry names are route.fallback.reason, route.latency.p95, route.cache.hit_ratio, route.fallback.count. we'll include that in the deck.
[06:32] Tom: what's the typical detection window? how quickly do you detect region degradation?
[06:37] Maya: health checks every few seconds, aggregated over short windows; default detection is 30s for aggressive failover, but you can tune it.
[06:45] Ian: okay, on the benchmark — what exactly do you need from us?
[06:49] Maya: if you can share a representative payload and concurrency targets for peak and sustained (e.g., 200 QPS peak, 50 sustained), we'll run with two regions, simulate a region fail at t+10min and show fallback metrics and logs.
[07:03] Ruth: we'll do that, Tom will put the spreadsheet together.
[07:07] Tom: yes. also can we get an estimate for data egress for multi-region replication?
[07:12] Ethan: we'll include an estimated egress cost table in the follow-up. depends on payload size and sync frequency; Private with VPC peering sometimes reduces egress cost.
[07:22] Lea: compliance: can you redact sensitive tokens server-side before logs leave the VPC?
[07:27] Maya: yes, we support server-side redaction hooks and can disable storing full prompts in hosted logs; Private gives you full control.
[07:35] Ruth: any known gotchas with on-prem HSM integrations? last time we tried something like that with another vendor the rotation process was kludgy.
[07:43] Ethan: two gotchas: network reachability and rotation automation. we typically recommend automating rotation with Vault or KMS and we provide scripts and docs. we'll share a sample rotation playbook and test harness.
[07:57] Ian: can Redwood do scheduled failover drills? we wanna test oncall and downstream behavior.
[08:03] Maya: yes, we can run chaos-style drills in staging; we have a chaos playbook and also a canary rollback demo we can run live or prerecorded.
[08:11] Ruth: cost question — Dedicated reserved pool price and delta to higher SLA?
[08:16] Ethan: price tiers vary. reserved capacity with 99.95% SLO and 24/7 support is a higher tier; we'll include a preliminary quote based on your QPS once you share the traffic spreadsheet.
[08:26] Tom: let's move to failure scenarios; here's our list: region outage, model regression (wrong outputs), sustained tail latency spike, and storage (cache) corruption. talk through each quickly?
[08:36] Maya: region outage = route failover to healthy region with cache warm-up; model regression = auto-roll to previous pinned model version and flag to humans; tail latency spike = reduce batch size and shift to quantized variant; cache corruption = invalidate and optionally serve from read-through to model with degradation window.
[08:59] Ian: for auto-roll, how long to revert? is there hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping in noisy signals?
[09:06] Maya: yes hysteresis — we need sustained error delta for a window before auto-rollback; you can set the window and thresholds. plus canary windows prevent immediate full rollout.
[09:18] Ruth: are there examples of customers who used Redwood to keep their app online through a cloud region outage?
[09:24] Ethan: yes, we have a case where an e-comm customer failed over across regions with <1% user impact; we can share an anonymized postmortem and metrics.
[09:33] Ruth: great.
[09:35] [~10:00 minutes into call — brief side discussion about procurement timelines]
[10:01] Ethan: what's your expected timeline for a pilot?
[10:05] Ruth: we'd like a 3-week pilot starting end of month if possible. security review needs to happen first.
[10:12] Ethan: understood — we'll prioritize the security pack.
[10:15] Tom: will you run the benchmark in our test account or your shared infra?
[10:19] Maya: we can do either. for Private-sized testing we prefer to provision a temporary dedicated pool in your VPC; for Hosted proof we can run in our sandbox and give you full logs.
[10:31] Ian: okay. couple quick clarifications about logs: retain for 90 days by default? can we push to our S3?
[10:36] Ethan: default retention is 30 days for Hosted, longer for enterprises; we can push logs to your S3 or a log forwarder in Private.
[10:44] Lea: and data residency again — ensure EU data stays in eu-west-1 for certain endpoints?
[10:49] Maya: yes we will enforce region pinning for those routes.
[10:53] Ruth: good. any blockers you see?
[10:56] Jordan: none. we just need the payload and traffic spreadsheet and we'll scope the pilot and quote.
[11:02] Ethan: cool, let's summarize next steps.
[11:05] [Recap]
[11:06] Ethan: we'll send the SOC2 + security pack, the fallback acceptance matrix, runbook template, sample rotation scripts, and a request for traffic/payload details. Maya will run the benchmark once we have payload. Sable will aim to deliver spreadsheet by 2026-07-20.
[11:22] Ruth: thanks, expect the spreadsheet.
[11:24] Ethan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark window and share the deck.
[11:30] [Meeting ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker overlaps and mis-recognized acronyms (SMAL for SAML, K-V cash for KV cache) present. Links shared during call: security pack (link sent afterward), runbook template (deck).
